title: Man. Post. Cap. X: PLAC — restates GAR’s major: death without own actual reatus ⇒ Adam’s reatus imputed
pass_a_gloss: Placeus restates the form Garissoles needs: where death reigns and there is no reatus from one’s own actual sin, Adam’s first-sin reatus must be imputed; before the law death reigned even over parvuli without own-sin reatus; therefore infants had Adam’s reatus necessarily imputed.
pass_b_english: Where death reigns, and there is no reatus from one’s own actual sin, there the imputation of the reatus of the first sin is necessary.
But before the law death reigned, even over those in whom there was no reatus from their own sin—namely, over little ones.
Therefore the reatus of the first sin was necessarily imputed to infants.
source_text: Ubi mors regnat, nec est reatus ex peccato proprio actuali, ibi necessario est imputatio reatus primi peccati. At ante legem mors regnavit, etiam in eos in quibus non fuit reatus ex peccato proprio, nempe in parvulos. Ergo infantibus reatus primi peccati necessario fuit imputatus.

choices.choice: Death without own actual reatus ⇒ Adam reatus imputed

notes: Cap. X Rom. 5:14 densify section 708 from locked 1661 Latin (pp. 370–372 tip, Rom. 5:14).
